INTRODUCTION TO PLC
A programmable logic controller (PLC) is a device that replaces the control logic used in systems or processes. 28 Volts Motor S1 K1
DISCUSSION
The same system or process that would require a great number of electromechanical relays is now performed by a more compact and versatile PLC.
PLC's do contain relays, but the PLC can easily be modified by programming instead of rewiring the internal circuitry and components..
In order to fully understand how the PLC controls a system or process, we need to look closer at its functions.
2. Central Processing Unit Input Central Output Section Processing Section Unit
The input/output (I/O) sections route all external signals into the central processing unit and direct signals from the central processing unit to the outside circuitry. Input Output Section Section
Different types of I/O modules are available such as TTL, relay and analog.
The central processing unit (CPU) analyzes the input signal and assigns an appropriate output. Input Central Output Section Processing Section Unit
The programming device is added when the PLC requires program modifications. Central Processing Unit Programming Device
Let's look at how these sections work together to control a system or process. Input Central Output Section Processing Section Unit
Most systems or processes use a manually activated switch to apply power. This switch is hard-wired to the input section of the PLC. 24V S1 Input Output Section CPU Section PLC
DEFINITION
HARD-WIRED - The term hard-wired means that the electronic components are physically connected and wired together.
All signals must go through the input section in order to reach the CPU. S1 Input Section
The applied 24 volts is converted to 5 volts inside the input section and sent on to the CPU for processing. 24V 5V CPU
The 5 volt signal sent to the CPU is converted to a "1" and stored in an input specific memory location. 24V 1 Input Section CPU
This condition (1) tells the CPU that someone has pushed a button and closed the switch. The CPU is now ready to perform the next step in the process. Input Section CPU
The CPU uses a 1 to pass information about the closed switch to an output specific memory location. 1
Once the 1 is loaded into the output memory location of the CPU a 5 volt signal is applied to the output section. 5V Output Section
All output signals from the CPU must pass through the output section before going to the rest of the circuitry.
The output section converts the CPU's 5 volt output to 24 volts before releasing the signal.
The output voltage from the output section is hard-wired to an external light. The output signal illuminates the light.

BASIC LADDER LOGICE
The PLC understands ladder logic like a computer understands a program.
DISCUSSION
If we intend to communicate with the PLC we need to learn the language it understands, like ladder logic.
Let's start by analyzing a basic ladder logic diagram and the symbols used.
Ladder logic diagrams use logic symbols to illustrate operations. Motor 1001 0031 S2 Heater 1002 0032 Operational Ladder Logic Diagram Diagram
Ladder logic diagrams use numbered input and output symbols to represent the devices used, like switches, relays, motors and heaters. Motor 1001 0031 S2 Heater 1002 0032 Ladder Logic Diagrammm
The diagram shows program statements as horizontal rungs between two vertical rails. Rail Rail Rungs S1 Motor 1001 0031 S2 Heater 1002 0032
The name "ladder" logic comes from the ladder-like appearance of the diagram and the rung/rail terminology.
Each rung has an input statement and an output statement. ngs Input Output Input Output

The output statement is executed when the input is true. In this example the motor turns when S1 is closed and the heater operates when S2 is closed. Input Output Input Output Input Output Input Output
WHITE HEAT
Here are the input symbols commonly used in ladder logic diagrams.

Examine If Open (XIO). The contact is normally closed and passes power until activated by an applied condition of 1 (ON). The contact is open (false) when the applied condition is 1, and closed (true) when the applied condition is 0.

Examine If Closed (XIC). The contact is normally opened and does not pass power until activated by an applied condition of 1 (ON). The contact is closed (true) when the applied condition is 1 and open (false) when the applied condition is 0.

LATCH INSTRUCTION - The LATCH instruction is used whenever a contact needs to stay open, or closed, even after the initial input is removed. The instruction energized the specified output point and this output remains energized until the UNLATCH instruction is given.
DEFINITION
Since B0 is true, rung 3 is true and the run LED illuminates. Rung 4 remains false since the contact is normally closed.
NORMALLY CLOSED - A normally closed contact is false (0) when the applied condition is 1.
DEFINITION

Pressing the stop button makes rung 2 true which unlatches B0. Since B0 is false, rung 4 is true and the stop LED illuminates.

The next part of the experiment lets you control the PLC trainer's motor and the PC card's LED's with the start and stop buttons.
Two rungs are added to the ladder logic program to control the motor.
When the start button is closed, B0 is latched making rungs 3 and 5 true. The run LED illuminates and the PLC trainer's motor turns.
The motor continues to turn and the run LED stays lit when the start button is released because B0 stays true.
Pressing the stop button unlatches B0 which makes rungs 4 and 6 true. The stop LED illuminates and the PLC trainer's motor stops turning.

The last part of the experiment uses a timer instruction to delay the start of the motor for 10 seconds.
The timer instruction replaces the old time delay relay used in electromechanical control systems.
Pressing the start button latches B0 making rungs 3 and 5 true. The timer starts since rung 5 is true.
The timer releases a high output to the done bit (DN) after 10 seconds. Since DN is true, rung 6 is true and the motor turns.
Pressing the stop button makes rungs 4 and 7 true which illuminates the stop LED and stops the motor.
